text:
B: Hiya! Oh, there you are. Can you hear me, love?
A: Yeah, I can hear you, hi! I'm Hodan, I'm in Wembley.
B: I'm Joanne, I'm in Batley, West Yorkshire. Oh, I'm ever so glad, I said to myself when I saw your photo, she looks like she gets things done. And I saw your laundry on the settee and thought, she's one of us.
A: Oh my God, you saw that! That's been there three days, don't judge me.
B: Judge you? Mine's on the stairs! Sorry, the landing. Anyway, what do you do? I saw the lanyard.
A: I'm a senior pharmacy technician, NHS, in the aseptic unit and the dispensary. I do the final accuracy checks and I run the rota. And I'm doing my accuracy checking qualification on top, because I want a lead technician post in the next couple of years, so I'm kind of doing two jobs at the minute, you know.
B: Gosh. And a little one as well? The lad in the photo?
A: Yeah, Idris, he's eight. It's just me and him, but my mum's ten minutes away, so.
B: Oh, mums are everything, aren't they. I pop round to mine every Saturday morning. What made you go into pharmacy?
A: Erm, I did Chemistry and Biology at A-level, then I had Idris quite young, at twenty-one, and I needed something proper, like a proper career, not just a job. So I got a trainee post and did the diploma while he was a toddler. Everyone thought I'd just sort of give up, and I didn't. So.
B: Well, good for you. Honestly, that's brilliant, that.
A: Thank you. What about you?
B: I'm an upholsterer. Self-employed, I've got a little unit. Chairs, headboards, the odd old settee.
A: Oh, that's cool, actually. Like the Repair Shop?
B: Don't get me started on the Repair Shop! I shout at the telly. They do in three days what takes me a fortnight.
A: Ha! It's all edited, isn't it.
B: It is. Anyway, I'm rambling. What do you do when you're not working, if you ever get a minute?
A: Gym. Three mornings a week, six a.m., before work. I did my lifts this morning, actually. I track it all in an app, I'm kind of obsessed.
B: Six in the morning! I do Zumba on a Tuesday with my sister-in-law and my knees were complaining for two days.
A: Zumba's hard, though, I'm not knocking it.
B: It's more of a laugh than anything. Do you cook, then, with all that going on?
A: Sundays. I batch-cook everything on a Sunday. Rice and spiced lamb, suqaar, a pasta bake for Idris because he won't eat anything else.
B: Oh, I do exactly the same! Sunday afternoon, everything in the freezer. Our Lewis comes for his tea Sundays and goes home with a bag full of tubs.
A: See, that's sensible. And then my mum does cardamom tea that's honestly better than anything you can buy, like, anywhere.
B: Ooh, I've never had that. Is it—
A: Sorry, go on.
B: No, I were going to ask, is it with milk?
A: With milk, yeah, and sugar, and you boil it all up together. People make it with a teabag and I just can't.
B: Well, you'll have to send me the—
